facts.text: Chanticleer is a 48 acre botanical garden on the former Rosengarten estate at 786 Church Road.
The estate was built in 1912 as a summer cottage for Christine Penrose and Adolph G. Rosengarten Sr.
Adolph Rosengarten Jr. set up a foundation to make the estate a public garden, open to the public in 1993.
Christopher Woods, a native of Britain, was hired to develop the garden.
Clark Park covers 9.1 acres between 43rd and 45th streets and Baltimore and Woodland Avenues.
The park was established in 1895 on land donated by banker Clarence Howard Clark.
It holds a life-sized 1890 sculpture of Charles Dickens.
It is home to the Shakespeare in Clark Park theatre company.
Cowan Park is named for Leslie Cowan, a Radnor resident killed in action in 1945 during World War II.
It has been one of the Radnor Township parks since the early 1950s.
Gulph Creek, dammed to form the Wayne Natatorium pool, runs through the park.
The Wayne Natatorium pool measured 500 feet by 100 feet and closed in 1903 after a drought.
Dilworth Park was rebuilt from Dilworth Plaza and opened on September 4, 2014.
Pennsylvania Railroad's Broad Street Station occupied the site from 1881 until its demolition in 1953.
Dilworth Plaza was completed in 1977 and named for Richardson Dilworth, twice mayor of Philadelphia.
The park has a programmable fountain that becomes an ice skating rink in winter.
The park is managed by Center City District on a long-term lease with the city.
Eakins Oval is named for Philadelphia realist painter Thomas Eakins.
The oval was part of Jacques Gréber's design for the Benjamin Franklin Parkway, proposed in 1917.
It is a traffic circle at the northwest end of the Parkway in front of the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

name: Edgar Allan Poe National Historic Site

facts.text: The memorial has three terraces and seventeen sculptures commissioned over thirty years.
Ellen Phillips Samuel left her estate in trust for sculptures emblematic of the history of America.
Sculptors were found through Sculpture Internationals held in 1933, 1940 and 1949.
Encke Park was the site of the Radnor Township Sewage Plant in the mid-1940s.
The township purchased the land in 1965 and it was formerly called Iven Field.
It was renamed in 1974 for Ethel G. Encke, founder of the Radnor Recreation Department.
Fairview Park is at 4418 Manayunk Avenue and has flower gardens, mature trees and a Tiny Library.
The Friends of Fairview Park formed in 2018 and removed the chain-link fencing.
Fenimore Woods is an 11.5 acre park at 1194 Eagle Road with a 3-acre fishing pond.
Valley Forge Military Academy first bought the land for a summer camp.
Radnor Township acquired the tract in 1973.
Much of the park is woods with three streams, a pond and marshland.
Francisville Playground opened in 1926 and sits on 3.7 acres.
It has a baseball field, two basketball courts, tot play areas and a recreation center.
FDR Park was originally named League Island Park and covers about 348 acres.
Olmsted Brothers designed the park.
The American Swedish Historical Museum (1926) is one of the remains of the 1926 Exposition.
The park was added to the Philadelphia Register of Historic Places in 2000.
Franklin Square is one of the five original squares planned by William Penn in 1682.
It was renamed in 1825 in honor of Benjamin Franklin.
Historic Philadelphia, Inc. refurbished the park from 2003 to 2006.
The park has a golf course, playground, carousel and gardens.
Girard Fountain Park is a 0.15-acre pocket park at 325 Arch Street in Old City.
It was created in the mid-1960s after four commercial buildings were demolished.
Volunteers now incorporated as Old City Green maintain the park.
The fountain was restored to operation in August 2008.
Gorgas Park covers 20 acres along 6300 Ridge Avenue.
The park was dedicated on July 4, 1893 by the city of Philadelphia.
Friends of Gorgas Park was established in 1997 to restore the park.
The park is a former industrial site turned riverfront park and trail on the Schuylkill River.
Groundbreaking took place in 2009 after a capital campaign.
